text.p: Turkish central bank heavily funded banks on Monday to meet fresh liquidity demand buoyed by mid-month public sector salary and pension payments as well as a forthcoming holiday, bankers said.
The central bank lent towards the close 22.3 trillion lira at 72 percent overnight, 23.5 trln lira at 67 percent tmrw/next and 8.1 trln lira at 68 percent tmrw/week.
The average overnight money rate jumped to 71.75 percent from Friday's 58.65 percent particularly due to heavy borrowing by state banks despite a 33.9 trillion lira cash surplus at the opening.
Markets will close for a 4-1/2 day religious holiday from mid-Thursday and reopen on April 22, to be followed by an April 23 national holiday.
The average overnight repo rate also rose to 74.64 percent from 73.27 percent in line with tight liquidity. The rates were highly volatile between 69-93 percent in the day.
Trade volume in the bond market was weak as players were sidelined ahead of the holiday, bankers said.

The most active papers were again April 22 and 29, 1998 which yielded 94.52 percent and 94.92 percent, down 0.37 and 0.15 percentage points, respectively from Friday. Yields in other papers were mixed in narrow ranges.
Turkish lira eased to 131,960 versus dollar compared Friday's close of 131,350 in line with the dollar/dmark parity.
The central bank's key dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers was raised to 131,900 lira from 131,800 at the opening and 131,300 at Friday's close.
